text:
maria: heads up — seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions in eu-west1-a. lots of tiny pods getting bounced, starts ~11:05 UTC.
kevin: :eyes: is this fragmentation or a network hotspot?
sasha: quick glance — NIC tx/rx on rack-12 looks pegged, kubelet evictions cite NodeNetwork pressure. also descheduler is reshuffling tiny pods into warm nodes then autoscaler drains them. messy.
infra-bot: [ALERT] Node gpu-node-12-3 reported HighNetworkUtilization at 2025-05-07T11:06:12Z — see metrics: https://metrics.internal/redwood/eu-west1/rack-12
maria: relevant snippet from node describe: ```bash
$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-12-3
Name: gpu-node-12-3
Non-terminated Pods: 12
Allocated resources: cpu: 32, memory: 256Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 8
Events:
  Warning  Eviction  4m (x3 over 10m)  kubelet  The node was low on resource: NodeNetworkUnavailable.
  Normal   NetworkThrottle  3m  kernel  tx_queue full, dropped packets
```
june: ack — I can see the tx drops on the NIC graph, peaks line up with checkpoint windows from the model-replicator jobs. those replicate shard snapshots every ~5m which floods the rack uplink.
liam: that explains the pattern. consequences: scheduler sees nodes as unhealthy -> taint applied -> pods move -> fragmentation increases. tiny pods with podAntiAffinity get stranded on non-GPU warm nodes.
kevin: short-term mitigation ideas?
maria: propose emergency steps: 1) reduce descheduler churn in eu-west1 for 30m, 2) throttle model-replicator replication concurrency on rack-12, 3) temporarily relax strict podAntiAffinity for small batch jobs so they can pack.
sasha: agree. also bump CA scale-up delay and scale-down-unneeded-time to avoid flapping while we stabilize.
june: I can run a canary for the descheduler toggle and throttling. schedule: canary on rack-12 only for 15m.
liam: config snippets for quick changes: ```yaml
# scheduler scoring tweak (canary)
kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1
profiles:
  - schedulerName: default-scheduler
    pluginConfig:
      - name: InterPodAffinity
        args:
          weight: 5  # lower from 10 to 5 to reduce anti-affinity strictness
```
and CA tunables: ```yaml
# cluster-autoscaler emergency patch
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-up-delay=3m
```
kevin: :thumbsup: can we also gate the model-replicator change behind a feature-flag so rollout is reversible?
maria: yes — replicator already supports --max-concurrency and a feature flag. I'll cut a patch to set --max-concurrency=2 for rack-12.
infra-bot: deploy started by june at 1768601301 (descheduler:disabled for rack-12 canary)
june: canary in progress. monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/eu-west1/rack-12/evictions
sasha: note on tradeoffs: relaxing anti-affinity will reduce evictions and improve packing (cost win) but increases risk of noisy neighbors for latency-sensitive model inferences. we should restrict to batch/replication jobs.
liam: long term follow-ups (to track): [A] isolate replicator traffic onto dedicated egress VLAN per rack, [B] implement per-node network QoS classes for model replicas, [C] revisit compact-packing scheduler plugin for GPU pools. I'll file these.
kevin: filing incident follow-up and action items, assigning to ops and networking teams. tagging @oncall.
maria: thanks all — keeping this thread to record the canary. update in 15m w/ eviction count and NIC error rate.
liam: tcpdump scheduled on gpu-node-12-3 at 11:12 UTC to confirm packet bursts.
infra-bot: canary completed at 1768601388 — evictions down 72% on rack-12 during window.
june: rolling the scheduler/CA changes cluster-wide after 30m observation if no regressions.
kevin: great work. we'll iterate on QoS + long term isolation next sprint. :rocket:
